name: Kashmiri Chai
description: Traditional pink Kashmiri chai brewed with green tea leaves, baking soda, aeration, milk and cardamom, then topped with nuts.
method: Add tea leaves, 3 cups water and baking soda to a saucepan. Bring to a boil and cook briskly until the liquid reduces substantially and develops a deep reddish-brown colour.
Add the ice-cold water carefully, then whisk or ladle the tea repeatedly to aerate it for several minutes; this helps develop the characteristic colour.
Simmer again briefly, then strain the concentrated tea base.
Return the tea base to the pan, add milk and cardamom, and bring to a gentle simmer. The colour should turn pink as the milk combines with the brewed tea.
Add sugar for the common sweet Pakistani version, or salt according to preference. Pour into cups and garnish with pistachios and almonds.
tips: The pink colour depends on suitable Kashmiri green tea, baking soda and thorough aeration; ordinary black tea will not give the same result.
Do not add excessive baking soda, which can give the tea an unpleasant taste.
storage: Best served fresh. Refrigerate leftover tea promptly and reheat gently once.
